about: Boxed-warning history of five US drug labels, as versions. 'effective' is the date FDA approved the labeling change (the approval letter says it is effective on the letter's date). 'notified' is the date of FDA's letter to the sponsor under FDCA section 505(o)(4), known then only to FDA and the sponsor; it is taken from the later approval letter. 'announced' is the first public date (FDA announcement or news release); when absent, the change is treated as public from its approval. Each first version is the original approval. 'evidence_first_public' is when the trial report behind a change first appeared in a journal (PubMed); 'signal_first_public' is FDA's first public notice of the safety signal. Dates and wording were checked on 2026-10-14 against FDA approval letters and labels on Drugs@FDA (accessdata.fda.gov), current labels in openFDA, and PubMed. Only boxed warnings are tracked here, not other label sections. 'terms' maps a boxed-warning risk to MeSH descriptors (checked with the NLM MeSH lookup service on 2026-10-14); risks with no close MeSH descriptor, such as 'mortality', are left unmapped rather than forced. Research data, not medical advice.

versions.subject: levofloxacin
versions.title: Boxed warning added: tendinitis and tendon rupture (S-052)

facts.quote: A Boxed Warning with bolded font and enclosed in a black box was added

versions.note: The approval letter refers to FDA's 505(o)(4) letter of July 7, 2008. FDA announced the class-wide boxed warning request on July 8, 2008.

versions.subject: levofloxacin
versions.title: Boxed warning extended: exacerbation of myasthenia gravis (S-058)

facts.quote: may exacerbate muscle weakness in persons with myasthenia gravis

versions.note: Treated as public from its approval; the 505(o)(4) letter of November 15, 2010 was known to FDA and the sponsor.

versions.subject: levofloxacin
versions.title: Boxed warning revised: disabling and potentially irreversible serious adverse reactions (S-067)

boxed_warning: disabling and potentially irreversible serious adverse reactions
facts.quote: the Boxed Warning ... revised to include information regarding the risk of disabling and potentially irreversible serious adverse reactions

versions.note: FDA's Drug Safety Communication of May 12, 2016 announced the change publicly the same day as the 505(o)(4) letter. The list of risks is the boxed warning of current levofloxacin labels in openFDA (checked 2026-10-14).

versions.subject: varenicline
versions.title: Boxed warning added: serious neuropsychiatric events (S-012/S-013)

facts.quote: addition of a new BOXED WARNING to the package insert

versions.note: FDA's 505(o)(4) letter of February 19, 2009 concerned suicidality-related events. FDA announced the boxed warning on July 1, 2009, the day it approved the labeling.

versions.subject: varenicline
versions.title: Boxed warning removed after the EAGLES trial (S-040)
versions.note: Pfizer's supplement of February 18, 2016 proposed the change on the basis of EAGLES (Anthenelli et al., Lancet, e-published April 22, 2016). FDA approved it on December 16, 2016; Pfizer announced the removal that day.

versions.subject: montelukast
versions.title: Boxed warning added: serious neuropsychiatric events (S-073)
versions.note: FDA's Safety Labeling Change Notification Letter and its public Drug Safety Communication are both dated March 4, 2020; the labeling was approved on April 29, 2020.

versions.subject: febuxostat
versions.title: Uloric original approval (NDA 021856, ORIG-1)
versions.note: The approval letter required a postmarketing trial (PMR 811-1) of whether Uloric raises the risk of serious cardiovascular outcomes compared with allopurinol; that trial became CARES.

versions.subject: febuxostat
versions.title: Boxed warning added: cardiovascular death, after the CARES trial (S-013)
versions.note: Takeda submitted the CARES results on January 19, 2018 (sNDA S-013). FDA first announced the preliminary CARES signal in a Drug Safety Communication on November 15, 2017; the trial (White et al., N Engl J Med) was e-published March 12, 2018. FDA approved the labeling, including the boxed warning, on February 21, 2019 and announced it in a Drug Safety Communication that day. No 505(o)(4) letter is cited, so no sponsor-only date is given.

versions.subject: tofacitinib
versions.title: Xeljanz original approval with boxed warning: serious infections and malignancy (NDA 203214, ORIG-1)
versions.note: Unlike the other drugs here, the label carried a boxed warning from approval.

versions.subject: tofacitinib
versions.title: Boxed warning extended: mortality and thrombosis (S-024)

facts.quote: WARNING: SERIOUS INFECTIONS, MORTALITY, MALIGNANCY AND THROMBOSIS

versions.note: The approval letter, signed at 5:10 PM on July 25, 2019, refers to FDA's 505(o)(4) letter of May 9, 2019 on thrombosis, pulmonary embolism and all-cause mortality with 10 mg twice daily in postmarketing study A3921133 (ORAL Surveillance). FDA announced the boxed warning in a Drug Safety Communication on July 26, 2019, so the public knew it one day after it took effect. FDA had first announced the safety signal on February 25, 2019, from interim results not yet in a journal.

versions.subject: tofacitinib
versions.title: Boxed warning revised: major adverse cardiovascular events added (S-031)

facts.quote: WARNING: SERIOUS INFECTIONS, MORTALITY, MALIGNANCY, MAJOR ADVERSE CARDIOVASCULAR EVENTS, and THROMBOSIS

versions.note: The approval letter refers to FDA's 505(o)(4) letter of August 23, 2021 on major adverse cardiovascular events, malignancy, thrombosis and mortality. FDA announced the required warnings on September 1, 2021, updating its Drug Safety Communication of February 4, 2021. The ORAL Surveillance report (Ytterberg et al., N Engl J Med) appeared on January 27, 2022, after the label had changed.
